threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success criteria, and responsibilities for the framework project.

messages.text: Team, welcome to the official channel for the 'Inclusive Hiring and Onboarding Framework' project. The main goal is to create a standardized, fair, and efficient process for everyone. I've attached the initial project pack for your reference. Let's start by confirming the scope and our roles. Please take a look and share your thoughts.

Thanks for kicking this off! I've reviewed the pack. The scope seems clear. For T1, mapping the current processes, do we want to include temporary and contract hires, or focus solely on permanent employees for this first iteration? Defining this will help keep A1 focused.

Great question. To keep things manageable and meet the 30-day deadline, I suggest we focus only on permanent, full-time employees for now. We can add other employment types in a future version. What does everyone else think?
I agree with the focus on permanent hires. We need to be careful with the legal definitions of contractors. Excluding them simplifies compliance significantly at this stage.
Sounds good to me. Focusing on permanent hires makes sense.
I agree.
Excellent, we have alignment. Decision: The initial scope will cover permanent, full-time employees only. Contract and temporary hires are out-of-scope for this phase.

Now for roles. The backlog in the project pack has suggested owners. Can everyone please review the tasks assigned to their role and confirm they are clear on the expectations? Specifically for T1 (Process Mapping) and T6 (KPI Definition).
The tasks for the HR Assistant role are clear. I can start drafting the interview templates and onboarding checklist this week.
I see I'm listed for T1. Is there an existing map I can use as a starting point?

Unfortunately, there isn't a consolidated one, which is the core problem we're solving. We'll need to build it by documenting the current state from different business units. Happy to sync up and help you structure the approach.

The tasks seem fine. A thought on T6: we should ensure our KPIs can distinguish between sourcing and onboarding effectiveness. Sometimes a high 90-day turnover is an onboarding issue, not a hiring one. We need metrics that reflect that.
That's a critical point. Let's make sure we capture that nuance when we define the KPIs in T6. Thanks for raising it.
The tasks for HR Manager are okay. I will look at them later today.
Ok, I understand. I will start on T1 then.
Great. It sounds like we have a consensus on the task ownership as laid out in the project backlog.
To summarize: Scope is confirmed as permanent employees. Roles are confirmed as per the backlog. Let's get started. Our first major checkpoint will be the process map from T1.
Understood. I'll have a first draft of the job posting templates (T2) ready for review by tomorrow EOD to get us moving.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate standardized hiring templates and inclusive guidelines.

messages.text: Hi team, as promised, here is the first draft of the 'Job Posting and Interview Toolkit' (A4) for T2. It includes a job posting template with inclusive language suggestions and a structured interview guide. I've also started a draft of the 'Inclusive Hiring and Anti-Bias Guideline' (A2) to align with this. Would love your feedback.

This is a fantastic start, thanks for the quick turnaround! I've left a few comments in the A4 doc, mostly minor suggestions on the scorecard section to make it easier for managers to use. The structure is solid.

In A2, section 3, the part about 'protected characteristics' needs to be more precise. We should list them exactly as they appear in the relevant labor laws for each region. Just saying 'etc.' could expose us to legal risk. We need to be explicit.

That's a great point. I've updated A2 to include a clear appendix with the specific protected characteristics as defined by current labor legislation for our key regions. I'll need the Legal Consultant to formally sign off on that section as part of T3's DoD.

The inclusive language suggestions in A4 are good, but we could strengthen them. For example, instead of just avoiding gendered pronouns, we should also check for subtle coding like 'rockstar' or 'ninja' which can discourage certain demographics from applying. There's a lot of research on this.
Excellent suggestion. I've added a section on coded language to A4 with examples of what to use instead. Thank you!
Looks ok but will managers actually read all of this? Maybe the guideline A2 is too long.

That's a fair concern. We can create a one-page quick reference guide as part of the training pack. But the full guideline A2 is necessary as a detailed resource and for compliance. Let's keep the full version and focus on making the training materials very practical.
I've incorporated all the feedback into A4 and A2. The links are the same. Are we ready to approve these versions for use in the pilot?
Yes, from my side they look great. Let's move forward with these. Decision: The standardized job posting and interview templates (A4) are approved for pilot use.
Pending the final legal review, the content of A2 is fine for the pilot.

Perfect. We'll consider that a sign-off for now. Decision: The inclusive hiring and anti-bias guideline content (A2) is signed off for the pilot, with the understanding that a formal legal review is still pending as part of T3.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize onboarding checklist, 90-day plan, and integration with payroll/HRIS.

messages.text: Morning all. I've drafted the 'New Hire Onboarding Checklist and 90-Day Plan' (A3) as part of T4. It covers pre-boarding through the first 90 days. I'd appreciate your review, especially on the touchpoints with Payroll and HRIS (T5). I want to ensure we're not creating extra manual work.

Looks very thorough! I like the specific callouts for remote hires. For T5, the step 'Day 1: Confirm bank details in HRIS' is critical. We need to make sure the data flows correctly to payroll before the first cutoff. Have we confirmed with the payroll specialist that this timing works?

Not yet, that's the key validation we need. I've highlighted that step in the document. I assumed it was feasible since it's an existing process, but with the new checklist, the timing and ownership are more explicit.
This looks like a lot of steps for managers. Are we sure they will do all of this? The 90-day plan seems very detailed.

It is detailed, but that's intentional to provide structure. We can frame it as a guide, not a rigid script. The goal is to make their lives easier by telling them exactly what good onboarding looks like. The checklist format in A3 should help.
Does the checklist A3 align with the process map in A1? We need to make sure the documents are consistent.
Good question. I haven't seen the final version of A1 yet. Once it's ready, I'll do a cross-reference to ensure they align perfectly. For now, A3 is based on the standard onboarding stages.

I've just spoken with the Payroll Specialist. They confirmed the Day 1 HRIS update is fine, as long as it's done by 3 PM. They also requested we add a step for the manager to confirm the new hire's cost center by the end of week one. Can we add that?
Absolutely. I've added the cost center confirmation to the 'First Week' section of A3. Thanks for checking that.
Great. With that change, I think we have our agreement on the payroll and HRIS touchpoints.
Any other feedback on the A3 checklist and 90-day plan? If not, I propose we approve it for the pilot.
Looks good to me.
Ok.
Alright, let's lock it in. Decision: The onboarding checklist and 90-day integration plan (A3) are approved for the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and monitor the pilot, including training and communication to managers.

messages.text: Team, it's time to plan our pilot (T8). I propose we partner with the Marketing business unit. They are hiring for three roles next month and their manager is keen to try new processes. Tentative start date for the pilot would be the first week of next month. Thoughts?

Marketing is a great choice. That timeline works well. I've already prepared the draft 'Manager Communication and Training Pack' (A6) for T7. It includes a short slide deck and a quick reference guide. We can schedule the training with their managers for the last week of this month to prepare them.
Is one business unit enough for a pilot? Maybe we should include another one, like Sales?

Good question. For this initial pilot, focusing on one unit allows us to provide high-touch support and gather detailed feedback. If we stretch ourselves too thin, we might miss important insights. We can always do a second pilot or a phased rollout if needed.
We should inform the legal consultant about the pilot so they are aware. The feedback we gather in A7 might have legal implications for the final rollout.
Correct. I'll send them a heads-up. Thanks for the reminder.

Also, I've drafted a short feedback survey for T9 to send to the candidates, hiring manager, and interviewers who participate in the pilot. This will be the primary data source for our 'Pilot Feedback Summary Report' (A7).
Proactive as always, thank you! So, are we all in agreement on the Marketing unit and the proposed timeline?
Yes, ok.
Sounds good.
Decision: The pilot will be conducted with the Marketing business unit, starting the first week of next month.
Now, let's review the 'Manager Communication and Training Pack' (A6) that was shared. Please add your comments to the doc by EOD tomorrow.
Sounds good. I'll be on standby to incorporate feedback.
Team, I've reviewed the training pack A6 and the feedback. The changes are minor. I think we can approve it.
Decision: The manager communication and training plan (A6) is approved for the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot feedback, agree on adjustments, and confirm final rollout plan.

messages.text: Hello everyone, the Marketing pilot is now complete. I've compiled all the survey responses and interview notes into the 'Pilot Feedback Summary Report' (A7). The key themes are positive, but there are some great suggestions for improvement. I've listed proposed changes in the report to inform T10.
Excellent work compiling this, the report is very clear. The suggestion to simplify the interview scorecard is spot on. Managers found it a bit too time-consuming. I support that change.
If we simplify the scorecard, we must ensure we still capture enough information to defend a hiring decision if it's ever challenged. We can't remove the compliance-related scoring criteria.

I agree. The proposed change in A7 doesn't remove any criteria, it just combines a few behavioral indicators into broader categories to make scoring faster. All compliance-related fields will remain untouched.

Looking ahead to governance (T12), the feedback shows we need a clear, simple way for managers to ask questions *after* rollout. A static FAQ page won't be enough. We should consider a dedicated Slack alias or office hours for the first few months. This would also be a great source for future improvements to the framework.
That's a brilliant idea. Let's add that to our governance model. We can document it in the 'Issue Escalation and Governance Checklist' (A8).
The feedback is good. So are we ready to roll out?
Almost. First, let's formally agree on the list of changes proposed in A7. Does anyone have any objections to implementing those updates for the final version?
With the clarification on the scorecard, I have no objections.
Hearing no other objections, we'll move forward. Decision: The list of framework changes based on the pilot feedback in A7 is approved.

Now for the final step. Let's set a go-live date. I propose a full rollout starting on the 1st of the following month. This gives us two weeks to implement the changes (T10) and communicate. We will use the governance model as documented in A8, with a quarterly review cycle (T12). Any concerns?
The timeline is feasible. I can have all documents updated by the end of next week. I'll also finalize the KPI sheet A5 so we can start tracking metrics from day one of the rollout.
Perfect. Then it's settled. Decision: The official go-live date is the 1st of next month, with the governance model in A8 confirmed for ongoing updates. This has been a great team effort!
